meta.note: Single source of truth. Every value traces to a v1.4 section. CSS and the Office theme are generated FROM this file — never hand-edited. If a value is needed that v1.4 does not define, that is a gap: log it, do not invent a token.

blue.role: Primary ground. Covers, dividers, statements, links.

ink.role: Night ground and primary text colour.

white.role: Reading ground — reports and print; panels on chalk.

accents.comment: Surface palette only. COL-06 (Fixed): never encode data in these.

pink.role: Hot counter-signal, accent bars, left rules
pink.ratioNote: ink text on pink — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

teal.role: Cool highlight, section headers on dark
teal.ratioNote: ink text on teal — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

violet.ratioNote: ink text on violet — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

butter.ratioNote: ink text on butter — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

coral.ratioNote: ink text on coral — measured against #0D0D0D, not pure black

chartRamp.comment: Data only. Four series maximum (DAT-04, Fixed). Direct labelling is the compliance mechanism (COL-12, Fixed) — decide labelling before colour (COL-11).
chartRamp.warning: Book ch04 measured: under protanopia series 1 and 2 render at 1.10:1 and the lightness order inverts. Do not claim this ramp survives all CVD.

neutralsRemoved.note: REMOVED 16 Aug 2026. #D8D8D8 #A6A6A6 #6E6E6E #4A4A4A were read out of v1.4 §12 where they render the GREYSCALE DEMONSTRATION of the chart ramp — the desaturated strip proving lightness climbs monotonically. They are a rendering artefact, not tokens. Promoting them into the palette invented four greys nobody approved.

colour.greysPolicy: There are no greys. Ink #0D0D0D, charcoal #2D2D2D, chalk #F3F3F3 and white #FFFFFF cover every neutral need. Anything between them is an invention.

charcoal.role: Secondary copy, captions, slide titles on light grounds.
charcoal.note: Moved out of grounds 16 Aug 2026. It was listed as a ground carrying textOn 'white' and the ratio 12.41 — which is charcoal TEXT on CHALK, not white text on charcoal. Right number, wrong frame. Nothing in the system uses charcoal as a ground.

theLaw.statement: Every accent takes ink text. Every ground takes the text colour its own token declares — white on blue and ink, ink on chalk and white.
theLaw.supersedes: 'Every ground is a white-text surface.' That is false for two of the four grounds: white text on chalk is 1.1096:1 and white on white is 1.0000:1. The per-ground data in this file was always correct; the memorable sentence was not, which is worse, because the sentence is what gets remembered.
theLaw.readThisNotThat: Read the ground off tokens.json. Never off a remembered sentence.

display.use: Covers, section dividers, the big statement.

h1.use: Break to two lines rather than shrinking.

h2.use: Tracking compensates for optical tightening as caps shrink.

h3.use: The floor. Caps stop working below 16pt.

scale.source: v1.4 Readable size rules + Decision Book ch03 worked example: 'Sizes across those four levels span only 32px -> 24px -> 18px -> 16px, a deliberately narrow range, because weight and space are carrying the distinction.' Nothing here is chosen; it is read off the two sources and expressed in em against the 16px base.

note.from: v1.4 footnotes and caveats — 10pt minimum, 10.5-11pt preferred

base.source: v1.4 Readable size rules — document body 12pt minimum AND preferred. 12pt = 16px.

rhythm.source: ch03 — 'section headings carry 3x the space above them that they carry below, so they attach to what follows rather than floating between blocks.'

display.source: ch03 — display and covers are the decorative tier, 'no meaning carried, no accessibility cost provided a text equivalent exists. This is where a house voice lives and it should be used hard.' Free by the Book's own rule, so this needs no decision — but it is named as decorative, not as a step.

label.why: v1.4's size table gives SLIDE labels (14pt min, 16pt+ preferred) and no document label size at all. The caps floor is stated as 16pt 'on screen'. At a 12pt document body, a 16pt caps label would be LARGER than body text, which no document does. This is the only type number in the system with no source.

capsFloor.note: Resolves the v1.4 §08 internal conflict (labels stated at 14pt minimum, H3 note states caps stop working below 16pt) in favour of 16. Adaptable.

slide.status: DECIDED 16 Aug 2026 — the measured geometry, snapped to a unit.
slide.why: The written 6% / 7.5% flat was a real decision flattened to a constant. What the decks actually do is vary the top margin by what leads the slide, and that variation is the mechanism that guides the reader: a kicker is small and quiet so it can sit high, because it is not the message; a statement needs air above it to land. Give the title the kicker's margin and the slide top-loads — the composition loses the breath that makes the rest of the system work. So the three steps stay, snapped to one unit so every value is a multiple (ch02, Fixed).
slide.footerNote: Reserved on EVERY slide, covers and closers included. The band is not there because a number is printed in it — it is there because in a physical room the bottom of the screen is the hardest place to read: heads sit in the sightline. That reason does not change when the number does, so it is one grid, not two (ch12, readability from the back of the room).
slide.symmetry: The footer band and the largest top step are both ten units, so a slide led by a full-bleed element sits in a centred band. That is a consequence of the unit, not a separate rule.

supersedes.note: Measured 3.87 / 6.67 / 13.33 land on 3 / 5 / 10 units within 0.13 of a percentage point. The measured 6.4% footer is rejected: it is what the old decks did, not what the room needs.

separator.colour: blue on light, teal on dark

accentBar.use: Above a pull quote only. The one decorative use.

scale.note: One base unit, .25em, everything a multiple. Short (9 steps) and non-linear — increments widen as values grow, because perceived difference is proportional. em so it scales with context, like every component. ch02, Fixed.

slideScale.note: Measured from the hand-built decks and recorded in joy.css, where it was defined and never used. Percentages of slide width.

direction.position: Minimalist. Bright colours as set out. Plenty of breathing space to let the message carry.
direction.principle: The joy comes from what we are up to, not from ornament. The decision layer keeps the message in check.
